title: Joe Washington: 1974 Unanimous All-American, Third in Heisman
question: Where did Joe Washington finish in the 1974 Heisman Trophy voting at Oklahoma?
answer: Joe Washington finished third in the 1974 Heisman Trophy voting after rushing for 1,321 yards as a junior, and he was a unanimous All-American that season. He placed fifth in the 1975 voting.
summary: Joe Washington (OU 1972-75) was a unanimous 1974 All-American and finished third in the Heisman vote. A look back at the Sooner running back's college career.
body: Joe Washington (OU 1972-75) arrived in Norman as one of the most electric backs in the country, and by 1974 he was at his best. As a junior he rushed for 1,321 yards, averaging 8.4 yards a carry, according to Heisman.com, and he finished third in the Heisman Trophy voting.

That fall also brought his first season as a unanimous All-American, as listed by the College Football Hall of Fame. Washington was part of the Sooners team that went undefeated and was recognized as national champion. Oklahoma was on probation and barred from television, so fans outside Oklahoma saw relatively little of him.

He came back for his senior year of 1975 and finished fifth in the Heisman voting, with 944 rushing yards. Heisman.com notes the Sooners were still off television, which probably hurt his Heisman case. Oklahoma again won the national title, giving Washington a part in back-to-back championships.

Over four seasons he gathered 3,995 career rushing yards and 5,781 all-purpose yards, according to the Hall of Fame. All-America honors came in 1974 and 1975, and the College Football Hall of Fame inducted him in 2005. The NFL career that followed has its own story, but in Norman Washington is remembered as one of the great Wishbone-era Sooners.
